results.title: Preview: Ipswich Town v Arsenal | Arsenal FC Official Website | Arsenal.com
results.content:
As for our hosts, summer signing Emersonn came off in the 3-2 victory over Crystal Palace with a quad issue. However, O'Neil said the Brazilian striker was likely to be rested anyway for our trip.

The striker is one of just three injury concerns for the hosts alongside Jack Taylor, who has a knee injury, and Azor Matusiwa, who has a thigh issue but could still be fit to play. Zian Flemming, who featured for Burnley in an earlier round, is eligible to play due to a change in rules by the EFL. [...] Image Widget

Jurrien Timber returned to the pitch for the second half in our win over Sunderland for the first time since the Champions League final in May. That was at the expense of Ben White, who was forced off at half-time due to an injury.

Cristhian Mosquera and William Saliba both missed the trip to the Stadium of Light as they continue to recover from their respective injuries. [...] “We’re going to give it our best go at home under the lights. I think we missed the opportunity against Liverpool. We played well, but it was already 2-0. We missed the opportunity to use the energy of Portman Road under the lights against a big side."

on Reid, Van Domselaar and Agyemang and if there are any more injuries:

October is in our minds somewhere, but we still have to look at how the new response is. Day by day, there is a plan in place, but that plan has been changed several times now. October will be great, but let's see where it goes. Daphne is working really hard in the background with the medical team. [...] They could. We have one more session left and then we're going to go through player readiness, different scenarios in the game, different qualities that we anticipate we need. Of course there's always a medical handover as well. They've come in and they're great players, both of them. They both have had disrupted pre-seasons, have been away from the team a couple of weeks and we just felt like it needed a little bit more time to get settled. ## MATCH-WINNING SWITCH

Mikel Arteta replaced Myles Lewis-Skelly with Bruno Guimaraes at half-time, and it proved to be an inspired decision. The midfielder added a little more energy, covering an impressive 6.26km during the second half, just over 1km more than the man he came on for. Statistically, the former Newcastle United skipper also ran with greater intensity too.

Make sure you don’t miss the deadline! Finalise your team by 6.30pm BST on Friday 18th September ahead Brentford’s match against Chelsea.

The biggest dilemma this week for most FPL managers is what to do with the yellow-flagged Joao Pedro (£7.8m). The Brazilian is the highest-owned player in the game but has withdrawn from his national team squad through injury. [...] There are a couple of cheap alternatives for those looking to replace Pedro, including his former-teammate Liam Delap (£5.5m). The Englishman scored last time out for Nottingham Forest. Another option is Thierno Barry (£5.6m) with Everton hosting an Ipswich Town side that have conceded seven goals in two away matches. [...] Brighton duo Pascal Gross (£5.7m) and Maxim De Cuyper (£4.9m)are proving to be popular purchases after returning 17 and 11-points hauls in the Seagulls’ 5-0 thrashing of Coventry. The latter, who is classified as a defender in Fantasy, continues to play out-of-position on the left-wing, strongly increasing his attacking threat. With Brighton coming up against Arsenal this week, both players will find it tricky to continue their recent form.
